# Machine interface

Use `proj --machine <command>` for automation. Human command output remains the
default. `proj capabilities` (also with `--machine`) reports protocol/capability
versions and supported command families without loading a project.

Protocol version **1** writes one JSON object and a newline to stdout. Both success
and failure include `protocol_version`, `cli_version`, `ok`, `result`, and `error`.
`result` is null on failure; `error` is null on success. Failures exit nonzero.
Broken output pipes cannot receive a complete object and also exit nonzero.

```sh
proj --machine capabilities
proj --machine --project . path get --label output
proj --machine --project . version get
proj --machine --project . yml read
proj --machine --project . build-dev
```

Successful queries return `{ "path": "..." }`, `{ "version": { "major": 1,
"minor": 2, "patch": 3, "dev": 0 }, "text": "v1.2.3" }`, or
`{ "validated": true }`. Configuration queries validate without returning raw
configuration or parameter values. Other existing command families reuse the
ordinary CLI in a noninteractive subprocess and return `{ "completed": true }`
only when that command succeeds. Unsupported command arguments fail; capability
flags explicitly report absent preview isolation, attempt/release records and
direct R/IDE parity.

Stable error codes are `invalid_arguments`, `project_selection_failed`,
`query_failed`, `command_failed`, and `worker_unavailable`. Messages are static;
raw config, environment values, command arguments and chained domain errors are
not copied into protocol errors. This transport reuses existing `anyhow` domain
handling tracked by issue87; it does not promise a finer domain-error taxonomy.
With `--machine`, help/version display requests return capability negotiation.

All command progress and child stdout/stderr go to stderr, streamed directly
without accumulating logs in memory. Machine mode closes child stdin and enables
noninteractive policy. Child logs are user/third-party output and are not a secret
redaction service; avoid printing credentials in scripts. No environment/config
dump is included in the machine result. Callers must keep stdout and stderr separate.

A failed publication can follow successful local analysis. `command_failed` is
not a rollback or retry instruction: inspect local state/diagnostics before retrying.
No analysis-free publication retry or successful release record is invented here.

## Read-only local remote versions

Current source adds remote versions to capability negotiation, independently of
the installed preview. Its successful result is an object containing versions,
an array ordered newest-first for archive layouts. Each entry contains version
(a leading-v numeric string), path (the actual physical directory), empty and
present booleans, and metadata_untrusted (the latest VERSION asterisk boolean,
or null for archives). An empty result is versions: [].

Present means a real directory exists, not that its contents match metadata.
Neither false nor null metadata_untrusted proves integrity. Failed queries use
query_failed without returning the raw path or filesystem error. See the
[command reference](cli/remote.qmd) for layout and missing-target semantics.
